rule: major counts if raised by >=2 of 4 blind reviewers (3 opus general-purpose + 1 argon)
prompt:
You are a blind pixel-art reviewer. Do not read any code or other files; look ONLY at the PNG boards listed below (open each with the Read tool; they are large, look carefully, zoom by reading them, do not skip any).

Context: 16px-cell hand-pixel chipset for a JRPG dungeon, 3/4 top-down view (you see the top surface of things and their front face; NO side faces / no isometric). Two themes: MAGIC TOWER (wizard tower interior) and OTHERWORLD (demon realm, violet-black). Each board shows: the item description (yellow line at top), a Beodeul reference image from the existing chipset that sets the quality bar (shown 1x and 3x) with an Actor1 person for scale, then two anonymous candidates X and Y: piece at 1x and 3x, the piece placed in a scene (animation frames shown side by side), and sometimes extra sheets (autotile 6x6 mosaics, irregular test maps).

Criteria, judge each candidate against them:
1. Reads instantly as the described object at 1x game scale.
2. 3/4 top-down view: top surface + front face visible, no side faces, no isometric skew, perspective consistent with the Beodeul reference and the Actor1 person.
3. Style matches the Beodeul reference: material shading instead of black ink outlines, similar contrast, detail density and pixel cleanliness (no noise, no orphan pixels, no banding).
4. Scale vs. the person is plausible; the object sits on the floor (contact shadow/base) rather than floating.
5. Animation frames (if any): change is visible, smooth, loops, no jitter of the static parts.
6. Autotiles: no visible seams or repeating grid, edges/corners join correctly in the mosaic and irregular map; floating-island underside hangs only below south edges.
7. Fits its theme (magic tower / demon realm) and is distinct from generic.

A MAJOR is a problem that would make you reject the piece for shipping (misreads, wrong view, broken seams, clashing style, ugly artefact clearly visible at 1x). A MINOR is a polish note.

Boards (directory /home/main/z-project/rpg-zzu-dt-arcane/qa-runs/dungeon-themes/panel/r8/):
other.ground.png other.void_edge.png

Write your answer as JSON to /home/main/z-project/rpg-zzu-dt-arcane/qa-runs/dungeon-themes/panel/r8/answer-1.json (use the Write tool) and also return the same JSON as your final message. Format:
{"items":{"<item id e.g. arcane.lectern>":{"X":{"majors":[{"problem":"...","where":"..."}],"minors":[{"problem":"...","where":"..."}]},"Y":{...},"pick":"X"|"Y","why":"one line"}}}
Cover both items. Be specific and honest; do not invent problems, do not be polite. Do not edit anything else.

majors.problem: Reads as uniform salt-and-pepper noise (bright violet single/double pixels scattered evenly over dark purple), not as cracked stone; no slab or crack structure is visible at 1x or 2x. This is exactly the orphan-pixel noise the Beodeul stone avoids.
Contrast of the speckle is much higher than the Beodeul reference's material shading, so the floor shimmers and fights the character for attention.

minors.problem: Glow veins are thin pink-violet strokes that barely separate from the speckle; they only show in a few variants and do not read as 'faint glow veins' in the plain scene.
Saturated blue-violet hue reads more 'arcane/magic' than 'violet-black demon realm'; the floor is not black enough.
Low overall contrast; at 1x the floor is a muddy dark plum and the crack network only becomes legible at 2x+.
Crack marks are short dashes of similar length and angle, giving a slightly regular woven/scratched texture rather than larger cracked slabs.
Ember veins are red-orange with a single bright yellow core pixel; they read as lava cracks more than 'faint glow', and the identical vein shape repeats twice stacked at the bottom.

other.ground.why: Y reads as dark cracked stone with no seams and calm shading; X is high-contrast pixel noise that does not read as stone.
